summary: Amrita Saikia, a scholar in Tibetology and other fields, completed a PhD at the Tata Institute of Social Sciences (2018–2022). She served as Assistant Professor at Woxsen University (2022) and Visiting Fellow at the German Institute for Global and Area Studies (2023–2024).

Amrith Krishna works in linguistics and Indology. He has held positions at the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur, University of Cambridge, IT University of Copenhagen, Oriflow, Uniphore (attested 2023), and Learno.AI (attested 2024–2025).
Amruta Barbadikar specializes in computational linguistics and Indology. She earned a Ph.D. from the University of Hyderabad in 2020 and subsequently held a post there.

Amy Heller is a Tibetologist and historian-archaeologist who completed her Ph.D. under Ariane Macdonald at the EPHE (~1979–1992). Her career includes posts at CNRS, INALCO (2014–2016), SOAS (2011–2013), and visiting professorships at Rome and Sichuan.

Amy L. Allocco works in religious studies and Indology. She studied at Colgate University, Harvard University, and Emory University (PhD 2001–2009). She held a post at Elon University (attested 2015).

Amy Paris Langenberg is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. She earned her PhD from Columbia University (~2002–2008) and served as assistant professor of religious studies at Eckerd College (~2014–2020).

Amy Sims Miller is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her BA from Wesleyan University and an MA and PhD (-2004) from the University of Virginia under David Germano, alongside studies with numerous traditional Buddhist teachers.

Amy Snyder Ohta is a specialist in linguistics and Japanology who studied at the University of California, Los Angeles (1990, 1993). She holds a post as Professor at the University of Washington (attested 2026).

Ana Agud is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Salamanca (PhD 1965–1978) and the University of Tübingen (~1972–1977). She became a professor at the University of Salamanca in 1979.

Anagarika Dharmapala was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied at institutions including St. Benedict's College and S. Thomas' College. He founded the Maha Bodhi Society in 1891 and the Maha Bodhi Society of India.

Anagarika Govinda was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a doctorate at the University of Freiburg and studied under Nyanatiloka Mahathera and Tomo Geshe Rinpoche. He founded the Arya Maitreya Mandala (1933) and taught at Visva-Bharati and Patna universities.
Anagarika Munindra was a Buddhist studies teacher who studied under Mahasi Sayadaw (1957–1966) and Satya Narayan Goenka. He served as superintendent of the Mahabodhi Temple from 1953 to 1957.

Anam Thubten Rinpoche is a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Tsurlo Rinpoche and has served as a teacher at the Vajrayana Foundation College of Buddhist Studies.

Anand A. Yang is a historian and Indologist who studied at Swarthmore College and the University of Virginia. He held appointments at Sweet Briar College and the University of Utah before becoming a professor at the University of Washington (~2002).

Anand Venkatkrishnan is an Indologist specializing in religious studies and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at Columbia University in 2015 and serves as Assistant Professor of the History of Religion in South Asia at the University of Chicago (attested 2026).

Ananda Guruge was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned degrees from the University of Ceylon and the University of London. He served at the NIEPA (attested 1970), CSU Fullerton, and the University of the West (attested 2012).

Ananda Kentish Coomaraswamy was an Indologist and art historian educated at University College London and the University of London (D.Sc.). He directed the Mineral Survey of Ceylon (1903–1906) and served as a research fellow and keeper at MFA Boston.

Anant Sadashiv Altekar was an Indologist and historian. He served as Professor at Banaras Hindu University (~1930–1949), University Professor at Patna University (~1949–1957), and Director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (1955).

Anantalal Thakur was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Calcutta under Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya and Satkari Mookerjee. He served as Professor at the Mithila Institute and Director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (1968–1971).

Anantanand Rambachan is an Indologist specializing in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of the West Indies, under Dayananda Saraswati, and at the University of Leeds, later serving as Emeritus Professor at St. Olaf College (~1985–2021).
